subject: Physics
cards: OCR-H556.THRESHOLD_FREQUENCY

Define the term threshold frequency.

[1 mark]

Threshold frequency is the **minimum** frequency (of the incident EM waves/photon) to detach / emit / remove / release an electron (from the surface of the silver)
Also accept: electrons
Also accept: photoelectron / photoelectrons
OCR-H556.PRINCIPLE_OF_SUPERPOSITION

State the principle of superposition.

[1 mark]

(When two or more waves meet at a point) the resultant displacement is (equal to) the sum of the (individual) displacements (of the waves)
Also accept: sum / total / net for resultant
Ignore: vector sum
OCR-H556.NEWTON_S_SECOND_LAW_OF_MOTION

State Newton’s second law of motion.

[1 mark]

**Net** force is proportional to rate of change of momentum
Also accept: “equal to” for ‘proportional’
Also accept: use of resultant or total for net
Also accept: symbols provided they are defined.
Not accepted: force = mass x acceleration
OCR-H556.ARCHIMEDES_PRINCIPLE

State Archimedes’ principle.

[1 mark]

The upthrust (on an object in a fluid) is equal to the **weight** of fluid (it displaces)
Also accept: a named fluid, e.g. water
Note: ‘fluid’ or ‘liquid’ must be mentioned at least once.
OCR-H556.PRINCIPLE_OF_MOMENTS

State the principle of moments.

[2 marks]

• for equilibrium
• sum of / total clockwise moments (about a point) = sum of / total anticlockwise moments (about the same point) OR net /resultant moment = 0
OCR-H556.COHERENT

State what is meant by the term coherent.

[1 mark]

Constant phase difference (between two or more waves)
Ignore: in phase
OCR-H556.PHASE_DIFFERENCE

Define the term phase difference.

[1 mark]

difference in degrees/radians/angle between points on the same wave or (similar) points on two waves
Also accept: how far out of step/sync or leads/lags for difference
Note: must be a comparison between points/waves
OCR-H556.INTERFERENCE

Explain what is meant by interference.

[1 mark]

The **superposition** of coherent waves
Also accept: ‘superposition of waves with a constant phase difference (at the sources)’
Also accept: ‘waves that superpose constructively / destructively’
Not accepted: ‘combine / meet / interact’ for ‘superposition’
OCR-H556.KEMAX

State what is meant by the quantity KEmax.

[1 mark]

Maximum kinetic energy of the emitted/ejected (photo)electron
Also accept: released/escaped
Ignore: KE
OCR-H556.STOPPING_DISTANCE_OF_A_VEHICLE

Define what is meant by the stopping distance of a vehicle.

[1 mark]

Sum of **thinking distance** and the **braking distance**
Also accept: the (total) distance travelled from when the driver sees a hazard to the vehicle stopping wtte
OCR-H556.CENTRE_OF_GRAVITY

A solid uniform wooden isosceles prism has a mass of 3.98 kg. Explain what is meant by centre of gravity.

[1 mark]

the point where the **weight** of the prism appears to act
Also accept: gravitational force / gravity force for weight
Not accepted: gravity, mass
OCR-H556.PRINCIPLE_OF_CONSERVATION_OF_MOMENTUM

State the principle of conservation of momentum.

[2 marks]

• total / sum of / net momentum before = total / sum of / net momentum afterwards or
• (algebraic) sum of the momentum before and after = 0
• provided there is no external force
Also accept: closed system
OCR-H556.LONGITUDINAL_WAVE

State what is meant by the term longitudinal wave.

[1 mark]
**Vibrations** or **oscillations** parallel to direction of travel of the wave / direction of energy transfer
OCR-H556.INTERNAL_ENERGY_OF_A_SUBSTANCE

State what is meant by the internal energy of the substance.

[1 mark]

The sum of the (random) kinetic **and** potential energy of atoms or molecules in a substance
Also accept: ‘particles’
OCR-H556.ELASTIC_COLLISION

Explain what is meant by an elastic collision.

[1 mark]

**KE** is conserved (as well as momentum)
Also accept: No KE lost
OCR-H556.HOMOGENEOUS

State what is meant by the term homogeneous.

[1 mark]

Uniform distribution of matter (everywhere in the Universe)
Also accept: density of Universe (approximately) constant throughout
Not accepted: references/idea of isotropic/”looks the same in all directions”
OCR-H556.ULTIMATE_TENSILE_STRENGTH_OF_A_MATERIAL

Explain what is meant by the ultimate tensile strength of a material.

[1 mark]
The **maximum** (tensile) **stress** a material can withstand (before it breaks)
OCR-H556.INTERNAL_ENERGY_OF_AN_IDEAL_GAS

Define the internal energy of an ideal gas.

[1 mark]

Internal energy (of an ideal gas) is the sum of the (randomly distributed) kinetic energies of the particles
Also accept: use of KE or Ek and atoms/molecules for particles.
Ignore: reference to PE (of particles)
OCR-H556.GRAVITATIONAL_POTENTIAL

Define gravitational potential.

[1 mark]

Work done per unit mass to move an object from infinity (to that point)
Not accepted: ‘work done on 1 kg’
OCR-H556.LUMINOSITY_OF_A_STAR

Define the luminosity of a star.

[1 mark]
The (total radiant) power (of a star) /AW
OCR-H556.ELECTRIC_POTENTIAL_AT_A_POINT_IN_SPACE

Define electric potential at a point in space.

[1 mark]

(Electric potential) is the **work** done per (unit) charge in bringing a **positive** charge from infinity (to the point).
Also accept: work done / energy required to bring a unit positive charge from infinity (to the point)
OCR-H556.CHAIN_REACTION

Describe what is meant by chain reaction.

[2 marks]

• More neutrons produced (from each fission reaction)
• Go on to produce further (fission) reactions / splitting (of nuclei) / energy
OCR-H556.ULTRASOUND

Explain what is meant by ultrasound.

[2 marks]

• Longitudinal waves
• With a frequency greater than 20 kHz
Also accept: 20 kHz and above
OCR-H556.NUCLEAR_BINDING_ENERGY_OF_A_NUCLEUS

Explain what is meant by nuclear binding energy of a nucleus.

[1 mark]

(Minimum) energy required to separate the nucleons (to infinity)
Also accept: protons and neutrons for nucleons
Also accept: energy released when the nucleus forms from the nucleons
Not accepted: mathematical descriptions such as (mass defect x c^{2})
OCR-H556.TRACER

Explain what is meant by a tracer.

[1 mark]

Material (introduced into the body and) used so its position in the body can be detected / function of organ can be determined
Also accept: “used to produce images” for “detected”
Not accepted: “trace” for “position detected”
Ignore: treatment
OCR-H556.IMPEDANCE_MATCHING

In ultrasound scanning, explain what is meant by impedance (acoustic) matching and how it may be achieved.

[2 marks]

• (special coupling) gel is used that has the same /’matching’ (acoustic) impedance as skin / body
• Reduced / less / zero **reflection** (at the skin)
Also accept: Z
Also accept: gel and impedance is the same / matching for two materials / mediums
Also accept: more transmission
OCR-H556.FARADAY_S_LAW_OF_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION

State Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction.

[1 mark]

(induced) e.m.f. is (directly) proportional / equal to the rate of change of (magnetic) flux linkage
Also accept: ‘rate of cutting’ for ‘rate of change’
Not accepted: current
OCR-H556.WORK_FUNCTION_OF_A_METAL

Define the work function of a metal.

[1 mark]

The **minimum** energy needed to remove an electron (from the surface of a metal)
Also accept: work done for energy
Also accept: photoelectron for electron
OCR-H556.SPECIFIC_LATENT_HEAT_OF_FUSION

Define specific latent heat of fusion.

[1 mark]

• Either
• (thermal/heat) energy required per unit mass to change solid to liquid **at constant temperature**
• or
• (thermal/heat) energy released per unit mass when liquid changes to solid **at constant temperature**
Also accept: energy per kg /energy of 1kg for energy per unit mass
Also accept: energy required to melt unit mass at constant temperature
Also accept: energy released when unit mass solidifies at constant temperature
Ignore: L = E /m unless letters are defined
OCR-H556.INTERNAL_RESISTANCE_OF_A_CELL

Explain what is meant by internal resistance of a cell.

[1 mark]

Resistance (which causes a loss of energy) as charges pass through the cell
Also accept: current passes for charges pass
Also accept: resistance inside the cell or resistance produced by materials or chemicals in the cell
Also accept: lost volts per (unit) current
Also accept: resistance which leads to a drop in terminal p.d. when current is drawn from the cell
Ignore: resistance of the cell
OCR-H556.R_4_3_1_KIRCHHOFF_SECOND_LAW

State Kirchhoff’s second law and the physical quantity that is conserved according to this law.

[2 marks]

• Sum of e.m.f(s) is equal to the sum of p.d.(s) (in a loop of a circuit)
• Energy is conserved
Also accept: total / σ instead of ‘sum’
Also accept: voltage instead of p.d.
Not accepted: ….sum of IR ….., unless I and R are defined
Not accepted: σE = σV, unless V and E are defined
Note: Expect ‘sum’ at least once in the statement
OCR-H556.R_6_1_3_TIME_CONSTANT

Define the time constant of a circuit containing a capacitor of capacitance C and a resistor of resistance R.

[1 mark]

time taken for current (or charge or voltage) to fall to 1/e **of its initial value**
Also accept: to decrease to 37% of its initial value
Also accept: to decrease by 63%
Not accepted: capacitance
Not accepted: to fall by (a factor of) 1/e
Ignore: time constant = CR
OCR-H556.R_6_4_3_BETA_PLUS_EQUATION

In beta-plus decay, a proton decays into three other particles. Write a nuclear equation for this process.

[2 marks]

• p → n or proton → neutron
• (p → n +) e^{+} + ν or positron + (electron) neutrino
Also accept: u→d or uud→udd
Also accept: β^{+} or 0/1 β or ē or 0/1 e (but not e) for e^{+}
Also accept: νe (but not ν̅) for ν
Also accept: 1/1 H for 1/1 p
Also accept: Where A/Z values are given then they must be correct i.e. 1/1 p → 1/0 n + 0/1 e^{+} + 0/0 ν
Ignore: A/Z values for the M1 mark
OCR-H556.R_4_4_4_STATIONARY_WAVE_APPEARANCE

Stationary waves are formed on the surface of seawater in a harbour as incoming waves are reflected off the harbour wall. An observer is looking at these stationary waves. State how the observer can tell that these are stationary waves.

[1 mark]

Appearance of nodes / antinodes
Ignore: the waves don’t move
OCR-H556.R_3_5_2_ELASTIC_CONSERVED_QUANTITIES

Two objects collide. The collision is perfectly elastic. State two quantities that are conserved in this type of collision.

[2 marks]

• momentum
• kinetic energy / total energy
Also accept: energy / mass
OCR-H556.R_4_2_2_EMF_PD_SIMILARITY_DIFFERENCE

The quantities e.m.f. and potential difference (p.d.) are both measured in volts, V. Describe one other similarity and one difference between e.m.f. and p.d.

[2 marks]

• similarity: (both are defined as) work done per unit charge
• difference: e.m.f. energy transfer from chemical / kinetic to electrical / electrically (working) AND
• p.d. energy transfer from electrical / by electrically (working) to heat
Also accept: energy (transferred) for work done
Also accept: work per coulomb (since not a definition) or joule per coulomb
Also accept: other forms for chemical / kinetic
Also accept: energy transfer from / work done on the charge carriers
Also accept: Energy transfer to / work done by the charge carriers
OCR-H556.R_5_4_4_GPE_DEFINITION

Define gravitational potential energy of an object at a point in a gravitational field.

[1 mark]

GPE is the work done in bringing an object from infinity (to that point)
Ignore: any equations
OCR-H556.R_5_5_3_CMB_ORIGIN

Astronomers can detect microwave background radiation coming from space in every direction. Describe the origin of the microwave background radiation.

[2 marks]

• Any two points from
• (During / shortly after) the Big Bang
• or
• (Universe was initially) very hot
• or
• (Universe was initially) gamma photons
• Universe expanded
• or
• Universe cooled (to 2.7K)
• wavelength of (gamma) photons subsequently increased
Also accept: radiation for photons throughout
Also accept: cosmos / space for Universe but not matter / everything
Also accept: frequency/energy of photons subsequently decreased
Also accept: wavelength of photons/radiation has redshifted
Also accept: wavelength of photons has stretched
OCR-H556.R_6_4_1_FORCES_BETWEEN_NUCLEONS

Deuterium is an isotope of hydrogen. A nucleus of deuterium has a proton and a neutron. Describe the nature and range of the two forces acting between these two hadrons.

[4 marks]

• Strong (nuclear force)
• Any one from: short-range / range of about 3 fm / attractive between 0.5 fm to about 3 fm / repulsive below 0.5 fm
• Gravitational (force)
• Any one from: long (infinite) range / attractive / negligible / follows inverse square law
Also accept: ‘gravity’
Ignore: any comments on the weak nuclear force
Note: Penalise any clearly incorrect statements. Implication that strong is always attractive will lose A mark
Note: Penalise any clearly incorrect statements
OCR-H556.R_6_5_2_COLLIMATOR_LONG_NARROW

A gamma camera has several important components including a collimator, scintillator and photomultiplier tubes. Suggest why the collimator needs to be long and narrow.

[1 mark]

Allows only those gamma rays / waves / photons travelling along axis (of the collimator) to get through (and reach scintillator)
Also accept: less fuzzy / clear image
Also accept: all the gamma rays / waves / photons are parallel / in the same direction (to each other)
Also accept: absorbs those gamma rays / waves / photons not parallel (to the axis of collimator)
Also accept: so the photons are travelling perpendicular to the scintillator
Not accepted: the gamma rays are travelling vertically, unless it is clear the collimator is also vertical
OCR-H556.R_6_5_2_TECHNETIUM_ADVANTAGES

The medical tracer technetium-99m is used in imaging organs such as the brain. Explain the advantages of using technetium-99m for this purpose.

[2 marks]

• Emits gamma (photons / radiation / waves / rays)
Any **one** from:
• (Diagnosing the) function of organ
• Detecting tumour
• Small half-life
• (Gamma rays) can be detected outside body / passes through patient / least ionising
• Position of tracer located
Also accept: for half-life is a few hours
Not accepted: injected into a patient / non-invasive
OCR-H556.R_4_3_2_ACTUAL_CURRENT_LESS

A student connects a calibrated 10.0 Ω resistor across a chemical cell of electromotive force (e.m.f.) 1.50 V. The student expects the current in the resistor to be 0.150 A. Explain why the actual current will not be 0.150 A.

[2 marks]

• Current less
• Cell has internal resistance or greater (total) resistance or p.d. across internal resistor or p.d. across resistor/10.0 (Ω)
Also accept: ‘lost volts’ / power lost in cell
Ignore: wires have resistance
OCR-H556.R_2_2_1_BALL_DIAMETER_INSTRUMENT

A student measures the diameter of a ball in different directions. The student’s results are: 2.43 cm 2.54 cm 2.59 cm. State the name of a suitable measuring instrument to measure the diameter of the ball.

[1 mark]

(Vernier) Calliper or micrometer (screw gauge)
Not accepted: rule(r)
OCR-H556.R_4_4_2_XRAYS_UV_SIMULTANEOUS

An exploding star in a distant galaxy emitted a burst of electromagnetic radiation. X-rays and ultraviolet radiation from this burst were detected simultaneously at the Earth. State why the X-rays and ultraviolet radiation from this burst were detected simultaneously.

[1 mark]

Both travel at the same speed / speed of light/ 3.0 × 10^{8} **m s^{-1}**
Ignore: travels at ‘c’
OCR-H556.R_3_2_2_PROJECTILE_MOTION_OTHER_CONDITION

A condition for projectile motion is constant vertical acceleration. State the other condition.

[1 mark]

• Constant horizontal speed/
• Constant horizontal (component of) velocity/
• Zero horizontal force (however expressed)/
• Zero horizontal acceleration
Also accept: any alternate wording
OCR-H556.R_5_4_3_ASTRONAUTS_WEIGHTLESS_FREE_FALL

Both the ISS and the astronauts inside it are in free fall. Explain why this makes the astronauts feel weightless.

[1 mark]

There is no contact force between the astronaut and the (floor of the) space station (so no method of measuring / experiencing weight)
Also accept: astronaut and the space station have same acceleration (towards Earth) / floor is falling (beneath astronaut)
OCR-H556.R_3_3_3_MAX_SPEED_WHEN_POWER_DOUBLED

A car of weight 9300 N is moving at speed v. The total resistive force, F, acting against the motion of the car is given by the formula F = kv^{2} where k is a constant. Changes are made to the engine of the car so that it can produce double the original maximum power. Explain why the maximum speed of the modified car is not doubled.

[2 marks]

• Power is proportional to the speed cubed /
• Max speed is proportional to the cube root of max power /
• power proportional to speed x kv^{2}
• Valid reference to the cube root of 2 increase in velocity for double power /
• Valid reference to factor of 8 increase in power for double the velocity
OCR-H556.R_4_4_4_HOW_MICROWAVE_STATIONARY_WAVES_FORM

The microwave oven heats the soup unevenly because stationary waves are formed inside the microwave oven. Explain how stationary waves are formed inside the microwave oven.

[2 marks]

• (micro)waves **reflect** from (metal) walls / sides
• (incident and reflected) (micro)waves **interfere** / **superpose** (to form a pattern of nodes and antinodes)
Ignore: reference to coherence
OCR-H556.R_4_4_4_WHY_STATIONARY_WAVES_HEAT_UNEVENLY

The microwave oven heats the soup unevenly because stationary waves are formed inside the microwave oven. Explain why the formation of stationary waves causes the soup to be heated unevenly.

[2 marks]

• antinodes have high / maximum amplitude or
• nodes have low / minimum amplitude
• energy transfer / heating is maximum at antinodes or
• energy transfer is a minimum at nodes (leading to uneven heating)
Also accept: intensity for amplitude
Ignore: maxima and minima points
OCR-H556.R_5_4_3_GEOSTATIONARY_CONDITION

A satellite in a geostationary orbit around the Earth appears to remain at the same point in the sky when viewed from the ground. State one condition required for an orbit to be geostationary.

[1 mark]

• Period equal to one day/24 hours/rotational period of Earth
• Or Rotation in same direction as the rotation of the Earth (on its axis)
• Or Equatorial orbit
• Or radius of orbit is approx 42 000 km
• Or height of orbit above Earth's surface is approx 36 000 km
• Or zero velocity relative to Earth's surface
Not accepted: 'is in the same place in the sky'
OCR-H556.R_5_5_2_NEGATIVE_ENERGY_LEVELS

Explain why the energy levels of electrons in hydrogen gas atoms are negative.

[1 mark]

**electron** bound to nucleus / represents energy **electron** must gain to leave the atom / total energy of **electron** in atom is less than that of a free electron
Also accept: ionisation level defined as zero as AW for 'represents electron must gain energy to leave atom / move up energy level'
Also accept: potentials for attractive forces are negative.
OCR-H556.R_6_3_3_TRANSFORMER_LAMP_FARADAY

The primary coil of a transformer is connected to an alternating voltage supply. A filament lamp is connected to the output of the secondary coil. Use Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction to explain why the filament lamp is lit.

[3 marks]

• There is a changing / fluctuating (magnetic) field / flux (linkage)
• (magnetic) field / flux (linkage) in **core** and **secondary** (coil)
• Statement of Faraday's law: e.m.f. (induced) ∝ **rate** of change of (magnetic) flux **linkage**
Also accept: 'the direction of the field oscillates'
Also accept: 'the core helps to link the flux to the secondary coil'
Also accept: 'equal to / ='
Also accept: This changing flux can be anywhere
Not accepted: just E = (-)Δ(Nφ)/Δt
Ignore: 'cutting of flux'
OCR-H556.R_6_3_3_SWITCH_OPENED_LAMP_FLASHES

Coil A is connected to a cell and a switch. Coil B is connected to a filament lamp. Both coils are individually wrapped around the same iron rod. The switch is initially closed and the lamp is off. The switch is then opened. The lamp flashes on for a brief time, and then remains off. Explain these observations in terms of magnetic flux.

[3 marks]

• When switch is opened, there is (rate of) change in (magnetic) flux (linkage) which induces an emf / current
• as the (magnetic) flux links to **B** which causes the lamp to light
• (Lamp off) at start / end there is constant flux / no change in (magnetic) flux (linkage for coil **B**)
Also accept: flux is cut by B
Not accepted: just a statement of Faraday's law
OCR-H556.R_5_1_2_MOTION_OF_PARTICLES_SOLID_LIQUID

A heater is used to heat water in a beaker. Before switching on, the metal heater and the water are both at room temperature. Describe the motion of the atoms of the metal heater and of the water molecules.

[3 marks]

Any **THREE** from:
• Atoms of metal vibrate (about fixed points)
• Water molecules have translational KE
• The motion of the water molecules is random
• Metal atoms and water molecules have the same KE
Also accept: particles for atoms / molecules throughout
Also accept: idea that water particles move past each other
Not accepted: idea that the water molecules have more KE than metal atoms
OCR-H556.R_6_4_3_IONISING_RADIATION_INFERTILE

To control insect populations, sterilised male insects can be released into the wild. They mate with females, who then produce no offspring, reducing the future population. Sterilisation can be carried out using ionising radiation. The insects are placed in a canister about 10 cm across and then deliberately exposed to a known dose of ionising radiation. Suggest why exposing an insect to ionising radiation may cause it to become infertile.

[1 mark]

(ionising radiation may) kill cells / damage DNA/cells/gametes
Also accept: mutation of DNA/cells / causes free radicals (that react with DNA)
Ignore: cancer or damages organs/tissues
OCR-H556.R_4_2_4_MEASURING_WIRE_DIAMETER

A student investigates the resistivity of a wire. The wire has resistivity ρ and diameter d. The student takes five measurements of the diameter of the wire. Suggest how the student made these measurements.

[2 marks]

• use (vernier / digital / dial) calliper(s) or micrometer
• (taking readings) at different positions / orientations (along the wire)
Ignore: take multiple readings
OCR-H556.R_5_5_1_SUN_NEXT_STAGES

Our Sun will eventually become a red giant. Describe and explain the next stages of evolution of our Sun.

[4 marks]

• Any **four** from
• reduction in energy released by fusion
• gravitational force is greater than that from radiation and gas pressure
• core collapses
• fusion no longer takes place in the core
• fusion continues in the shell around the core
• outer layers of star expand and cool
• outer layers are released
• reference to planetary nebula
• reference to **white** dwarf (left as remnant hot core)
Ignore: current or previous stages of the Sun’s evolution
OCR-H556.R_5_5_2_ALGOL_DIFFERENT_TEMPERATURES

Suggest how an astronomer using just an optical telescope can deduce that the three stars of Algol have different surface temperatures.

[1 mark]
From their (different) colours
OCR-H556.R_5_5_3_HYDROGEN_LINES_RED_SHIFT

Suggest why hydrogen spectral lines play an important role in determining red shift of galaxies.

[1 mark]

(Relative) abundance of hydrogen (AW)
Also accept: ‘Hydrogen commonly found in stars’ (AW)
OCR-H556.R_3_5_2_INELASTIC_CONSERVED_QUANTITIES

A comet makes an inelastic collision with a small asteroid in space. State two physical quantities conserved in this collision.

[1 mark]

Any **two** from: momentum, (total) energy and mass
Not accepted: kinetic energy
OCR-H556.R_3_5_1_WEIGHT_THIRD_LAW_PARTNER

The weight of the ball is W and the normal contact force on the ball is N. According to Newton’s third law of motion, W is one of the forces in a pair of equal and opposite forces. Name the object that experiences a force of magnitude W but in the opposite direction to W.

[1 mark]

Earth
Also accept: planet / ground
OCR-H556.R_6_5_1_XRAY_ANODE_ROTATES

X-rays are used for diagnostic imaging in a hospital. Suggest why the anode is made to rotate.

[1 mark]

Cooling / preventing melting (of anode)
Not accepted: just ‘so the same spot isn’t hit all the time’
OCR-H556.R_4_2_4_VARIABLE_RESISTOR_QUANTITY

A battery is connected to a variable resistor. The variable resistor is made from a length of wire. The resistance of the variable resistor is R. State which physical quantity of the variable resistor is changed to alter its resistance.

[1 mark]
length (of wire)
OCR-H556.R_4_5_3_ELECTRON_WAVE_EVIDENCE

State one piece of evidence for the wave-like behaviour of electrons.

[1 mark]
Diffraction (of electrons by matter)
OCR-H556.R_4_2_2_EMF_PD_SIMILARITY

Potential difference (p.d.) and electromotive force (e.m.f.) can both be defined in terms of transfer of energy per unit charge. State one other similarity between p.d. and e.m.f.

[1 mark]

Both measured in Volts / same units
Also accept: V for volt
Also accept: they are both voltages/they are both measured with a voltmeter
OCR-H556.R_4_4_1_COMPRESSIONS_RAREFACTIONS

Sound waves in air are longitudinal waves consisting of compressions and rarefactions. Explain how the movement of air molecules creates compressions and rarefactions.

[3 marks]

• Molecules vibrate/oscillate
• oscillations parallel to the **direction** of the energy transfer / propagation
• Creating areas of high **and** low pressure
• Or
• regions where the molecules are closer together **and** further apart
Also accept: particles throughout
Also accept: move back and forth
Also accept: parallel to the direction of the wave
Also accept: areas are high concentration/density and low concentration/density of molecules
Not accepted: ref. to varying amplitude
OCR-H556.R_4_4_1_SOUND_NOT_POLARISED

State why sound waves cannot be polarised.

[1 mark]
It is longitudinal
OCR-H556.R_4_4_1_LONGITUDINAL_VS_TRANSVERSE

Describe the difference between longitudinal and transverse waves.

[2 marks]

• Transverse: **vibrations** /**oscillations** are perpendicular / right angles to the direction of travel / energy transfer (AW)
• Longitudinal: **vibrations** /**oscillations** are parallel to / in the same direction as the direction of travel / energy transfer (AW)
Also accept: 1 mark for ‘For one of the waves, the oscillations / vibrations are at right angles and for the other they are parallel to the direction of travel’ (AW)
Also accept: 1 mark for transverse (waves) can be polarised ORA
Not accepted: move for vibrations / oscillations
OCR-H556.R_3_2_3_CONDITIONS_FOR_EQUILIBRIUM

State the two conditions for an object to be in equilibrium.

[3 marks]

• Sum of the forces / net / resultant force (in any direction) = 0
• Sum of the moments / net / resultant moment (about any point) = 0
• Sum of the forces **in any direction** = 0 and
• Sum of the moments /torques **about any point** = 0
Also accept: (total) upward force = (total) downwards force
Also accept: (total) clockwise moment = (total) anticlockwise moment
Also accept: torque for moment
OCR-H556.R_4_5_2_PHOTOELECTRON_EMISSION

Electromagnetic radiation is incident on a metal plate. Photoelectrons are emitted. State why electrons are emitted.

[1 mark]

Any one from:
• The **energy** from **photons** is absorbed by (photo)electrons
• The **energy** of a **photon** is greater than the work function
OCR-H556.R_5_1_2_PHASE_CHANGE_INTERNAL_ENERGY

A fixed mass of nitrogen changes phase from liquid to gas at a constant temperature. Explain the change in the total internal energy of nitrogen.

[2 marks]

• Kinetic energy of particles is constant **and** the potential energy increases.
• internal energy has increased (as the internal energy = KE + PE)
